session.summary: The session outlines a vision for FTFM (Facts Truth Fact Machine) - a revolutionary journalistic database system that records and structures news events, statements, and public records beyond traditional reporting. The concept aims to create a searchable, dynamic knowledge repository capable of tracking narrative changes, political promises, and accountability metrics over time with AI-powered analysis.

records.content: FTFM (Facts Truth Fact Machine) is a revolutionary journalistic database system that structures news as data rather than articles. The system records events, statements, and public actions in structured JSON format with entity relationships, enabling accountability tracking and pattern recognition that traditional reporting cannot achieve.

details.title: FTFM Core Concept: Structured Journalism Database
details.notes: This represents a paradigm shift from reporting news to recording and structuring news as queryable data. The innovation isn't in summarizing news but in creating a structured historical record of public events and statements.
details.completion_criteria: Working proof of concept that demonstrates the structured recording of news events with relationship mapping

project.goal: Create a proof of concept for a structured journalistic database system

records.content: Define the Minimum Viable Proof of Concept for FTFM, considering options such as mapping Glenn Greenwald's podcasts over a six-month period or combining multiple sources with entity extraction and claim tracking.

details.title: Define FTFM MVP Scope
details.notes: Consider testing with a limited dataset from established sources to demonstrate the concept without requiring extensive data collection initially.
details.completion_criteria: Written MVP specification with clear scope, data sources, and expected deliverables

project.goal: Create a clearly defined scope for FTFM's initial proof of concept

records.content: Acquire transcripts of one or two Glenn Greenwald podcasts as initial test data for the FTFM prototype, then develop a model to batch process them into structured JSON records with entity extraction.

details.title: Acquire Test Transcripts and Develop Initial Processing Model
details.notes: This initial step will help validate the concept by demonstrating how unstructured spoken content can be transformed into structured data objects with semantic meaning.
details.completion_criteria: Working prototype that converts podcast transcripts into structured JSON with proper entity extraction

project.goal: Build initial data processing pipeline for transforming unstructured content to structured records

records.content: The technical architecture for FTFM consists of a backend database storing structured JSON records with entity relationships, embeddings for semantic search, and a frontend that translates these records into Markdown files viewable in Obsidian. A synchronization layer maintains consistency between both systems.

details.title: FTFM Technical Architecture
details.notes: The hybrid architecture with structured backend and Obsidian-compatible frontend leverages both database capabilities and the flexible knowledge management features of Obsidian. Consider implementing vector search capabilities for advanced querying.
details.completion_criteria: Detailed technical specification document with architecture diagrams and component descriptions

project.goal: Design a comprehensive and scalable technical architecture for FTFM

records.content: Implement temporal tracking for all FTFM records to monitor how long statements remain valid or unchallenged, creating a 'statement half-life' metric for accountability. This adds a crucial time dimension to political and public statements.

details.title: Temporal Dimension and Statement Half-Life Metrics
details.notes: This feature would create a unique accountability measure not found in traditional journalism by tracking the lifecycle of statements and promises.
details.completion_criteria: Implementation of temporal tracking with visual representation of statement validity over time

project.goal: Develop temporal tracking and statement half-life functionality for FTFM

records.content: Develop 'Narrative Collision Detection' for FTFM - an automated system that flags when previously separate narrative threads suddenly intersect, such as when a politician who opposed certain interests suddenly receives funding from those same entities.

details.title: Narrative Collision Detection System
details.notes: This feature represents a breakthrough in automated investigative journalism by detecting meaningful pattern changes without being explicitly programmed to look for specific connections.
details.completion_criteria: Working algorithm that can identify and flag significant narrative intersections and contradictions

project.goal: Create an automated system for detecting significant narrative pattern changes and contradictions

related_items: Temporal Dimension and Statement Half-Life Metrics

records.content: Implement a dynamic credibility scoring system for FTFM that evolves based on how often claims from specific sources are later validated or contradicted by independent confirmations, creating an emergent reputation system based on track record rather than perceived authority.

details.title: Dynamic Credibility Scoring System
details.notes: This approach would be groundbreaking compared to static media bias charts by creating a living, evolving measure of reliability based on actual historical accuracy.
details.completion_criteria: Functional system that tracks claim validity over time and adjusts source credibility scores accordingly

project.goal: Develop a dynamic credibility evaluation system based on historical accuracy

related_items: Temporal Dimension and Statement Half-Life Metrics

records.content: Create a community annotation layer for FTFM where verified domain experts can contribute specialized knowledge and fact-checking to specific claims within their expertise areas, creating a living fact-check environment while preserving original claims.

details.title: Expert Community Annotation Layer
details.notes: This feature could significantly enhance the value and accuracy of the system while building a community of engaged experts, though it would require careful verification and moderation systems.
details.completion_criteria: Working annotation system with expert verification and moderation capabilities

project.goal: Design and implement an expert annotation system for ongoing fact verification

records.content: Implement a hybrid architecture for FTFM using blockchain-inspired approaches for high-value records requiring immutability, while maintaining traditional databases for speed and efficiency of the main system, creating the best of both worlds.

details.title: Hybrid Blockchain-Inspired Architecture
details.notes: This approach could provide tamper-proof guarantees for particularly significant records while avoiding the performance and scaling issues of full blockchain implementations.
details.completion_criteria: Technical specification and prototype implementation of hybrid storage architecture

project.goal: Design a hybrid storage architecture that provides both immutability and performance

records.content: Develop a mobile interface for FTFM that allows journalists and citizens to contribute real-time data through voice recordings that are automatically transcribed, entity-extracted, and incorporated into the database, creating a distributed accountability network.

details.title: FTFM Mobile Voice Contribution Interface
details.notes: This feature could dramatically scale data collection capabilities by leveraging distributed participants, though it would require robust verification systems to maintain data quality.
details.completion_criteria: Working mobile application with voice recording, transcription and submission capabilities

project.goal: Create a mobile interface for distributed real-time data contribution

records.content: FTFM represents a shift in journalism from merely reporting events to creating a structured, permanent record of public life. Unlike traditional reporting or even Wikipedia, which focuses on static information, FTFM aims to create a comprehensive, searchable record of day-to-day developments in politics, policy, and public statements.

details.title: The Philosophy of FTFM: From Reporting to Recording
details.notes: This conceptual foundation distinguishes FTFM from other news innovation projects that focus primarily on summarization or presentation rather than fundamental restructuring of how information is stored and accessed.

records.content: Create FTFM project organizational files including Contents.md as a main overview document and Tasks.md to track all actionable items related to the project with their statuses, priorities, and deadlines.

details.title: Create FTFM Project Organizational Files
details.notes: These files will establish the foundation for organizing all FTFM-related tasks, ideas, and documents in a coherent structure that can evolve with the project.
details.completion_criteria: Creation of _Contents.md and _Tasks.md with proper structure and initial content

project.goal: Establish organizational structure for FTFM project documentation

records.content: FTFM represents a revolutionary approach to journalism by creating a structured data layer for news events rather than just textual reports. The system aims to record public statements, policy changes, financial connections, and other significant events in a format that enables pattern recognition, accountability tracking, and historical analysis beyond what traditional journalism can provide.

details.title: Reflection on FTFM's Transformative Potential
details.notes: This project goes beyond existing news innovation initiatives by reimagining the fundamental structure of how journalistic information is stored, retrieved and analyzed. The potential impact on public accountability could be significant.
